subject: Cross-region egress safeguards & conditional failover discussion
messages:
From: Zara Khan <zara.khan@acmecorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Clarification: cross-region processing and temporary egress for failover

Hi Soojin + team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security and architecture teams:

- We need a clear statement on whether PII-containing inference requests originating in our EU region may ever be routed to a non-EU host during transient failover or load bursts (e.g., to the US or APAC).
- If transient cross-region processing is possible, what controls exist to limit the scope (time window, token-level masking, KV cache lifetime)?
- We also want to confirm KMS behaviour: are customer keys used for encryption of model inputs/outputs egressed during failover, and if so, what key material remains in-region?

I've attached our standard questionnaire to speed things up. Can you fill the highlighted sections about "transient egress" and "audit evidence"? If this needs legal/ops input, please loop them in.

Appreciate a short write-up we can attach to our procurement DPA review. If possible, we'd like a version we can put into our security review packet by end of day Thursday (20 Aug).

Best,
Zara Khan
Head of Security Engineering, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme-region-questionnaire.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification: cross-region processing and temporary egress for failover

Hi Zara — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. I've gone through the highlighted items and sketched an operational summary below; attaching an architecture diagram and an internal playbook excerpt for visibility.

Short answer (TL;DR): by default we serve requests within the pinned region you choose. Temporary cross-region processing is supported only under explicit, policy-governed conditions (capacity failover, regional outage, or scheduled maintenance). When it occurs:

- Duration: egressed data is kept transiently in non-pinned region(s) for the duration of the request and for up to 30 minutes for KV cache reconciliation. We can shorten that window to 0 minutes on request for customers that require no transient caching.
- Scope controls: we support per-customer failover policies that restrict which model variants and which GPU pools are eligible to accept egressed traffic (e.g., block non-quantized models from failing over).
- Key handling: if customer-managed KMS is enabled, input/output payloads are encrypted with the customer key before transit. Key usage logs are stored in-region and the key never leaves the customer's KMS boundary; only ciphertext is transported during failover.
- Auditability: every cross-region request is tagged with a transient routing flag and logged with token counts, source region, destination region, and the triggering condition. Logs are available via Console and exported to your SIEM (we can supply a sample log export).

Operational options we recommend for Acme:
1) Strict pin with emergency exception: default pin to EU with a documented SLA-backed exception that allows failover to a small allowlist (us-west1, europe-west3) and 15-minute cache TTL.
2) No-transient-cache configuration: disables KV caching and ensures per-request stateless routing; useful for high-sensitivity workloads.
3) Dedicated VPC private deployment: for full in-region enforcement and network egress controls (on-prem/VPC where failover stays within your cloud tenant).

Attachments: regional-egress-diagram.png (visual flow), pinning-ops-playbook.pdf (ops steps and playbook extract).

I'll follow up with Rishi from Legal on proposed DPA language/tight wording for the exception (draft clause suggestion). Let me know if you want the 0-minute cache option toggled for your account before Thursday.

Thanks,

--

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Zara Khan <zara.khan@acmecorp.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: cross-region processing and temporary egress for failover

Hi Zara — looping in Legal/Privacy comments as requested. Per Soojin's summary, we propose the following contractual guardrails to appear as an addendum to the DPA:

1) Conditional Failover Clause (draft): Redwood will route requests outside the pinned region only in response to (a) documented regional outage; (b) customer-approved capacity overflow policies; or (c) scheduled maintenance with >=48 hours notice. The addendum will enumerate the allowlist of alternate regions and the maximum transient cache window.

2) Key and Ciphertext Statement: when customer-managed KMS is used, Redwood will not have access to plaintext under normal operation. Ciphertext may be transmitted to alternate regions during conditional failover; key material remains in the customer's KMS scope.

3) Audit & Notice: Redwood will emit real-time audit entries for any conditional failover event and notify the designated security contact within 1 hour of occurrence. Full event records (including token-level counts and destination region) will be made available for 90 days.

I've attached a redline of the DPA addendum with the proposed language and placeholders for the allowlist and TTL. If that looks OK to Acme security, we can surface the addendum via DocuSign for your signatures (link below).

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/EXAMPLE-123456789
Attachment: DPA-addendum-redline.docx

If Acme prefers the stricter option (no transient cache and no cross-region failover under any conditions), we can convert that into a reserved-capacity Private deployment quote. Happy to discuss tradeoffs on a quick call — I have 30–11am PT free tomorrow.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarification: cross-region processing and temporary egress for failover

Thanks all — this is helpful. Quick points:

- Acme is OK with the Conditional Failover Clause provided the allowlist is limited and the TTL is capped at 15 minutes. Please set the default allowlist to europe-west3 and us-west1; we'll request exceptions if needed.
- We'll enable customer-managed KMS for the pilot and expect the key-restriction language verbatim in the addendum.
- Please send the DocuSign once Rishi's redline includes the 15-minute TTL and the two-region allowlist. Our legal counsel will review, but this should enable procurement to move forward.

I've attached the signed LOI and marked a couple of questionnaire cells for Soojin to confirm the 15-minute option. Also, we'll take the 30–11am PT slot tomorrow for a short kickoff call.

Best,
Zara
